classification.habitat: Open grassland, field margins and cultivated areas in warm climates
classification.distribution: Widely distributed and cultivated in India and tropical Asia

identification.description: A strongly bitter, erect herb with opposite leaves and small pale flowers marked with darker purple lines.
identification.stem: Green, erect, quadrangular to angular and branched stem.
identification.leaf: Simple opposite lanceolate to linear-lanceolate leaves with entire margins.
identification.flower: Small flowers in terminal/axillary panicles, usually whitish with darker markings.
identification.fruit: Slender linear-oblong capsule containing numerous small seeds.
identification.seed: Small numerous seeds enclosed in the capsule.
identification.bark: Not applicable as a distinct medicinal bark character.

dosha.kapha: not specifically documented in imported dataset

modern_information.evidence_summary: Andrographis paniculata is widely studied as a bitter medicinal herb. Modern findings should be interpreted by preparation and clinical endpoint rather than generalized as proven treatment.
modern_information.safety_notes: Verify preparation and dose from authoritative references; avoid self-treatment of fever or liver disease.

teaching_points: Demonstrate opposite leaves and terminal inflorescences.

practical_points: Observe leaf arrangement, flower markings and capsule shape.
